headline: South Asia: Pakistan conducted strikes at 10 locations in Afghanistan in response to recent drone attacks: info minister
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistan conducted strikes at 10 locations in Afghanistan in response to recent drone attacks: info minister.
- Asia: 8 killed in Russian strikes on Ukraine, maternity clinic damaged.
- Africa: Fighting intensifies in northern Ethiopia as Tigray rebels declare full-blown war.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
- Military Times, 6 hours ago: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
Unauthorized users accessed files containing the personal information of U.S. military personnel, a new breach notification letter warns.
- Military Times, 22 hours ago: Army awards Palantir $48.1M to modernize ammo management.
The tech company has built AI software designed to process data for targeting and decision-making, and now, managing ammo.
- Military Times, 5 hours ago: 8 sailors attempted suicide aboard ships from Lincoln strike group, Cao says.
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao confirmed that eight sailors from the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group attempted suicide.
- Military Times, 6 hours ago: Nellis Air Force Base says goodbye to last A-10 Thunderbolt II.
After five decades at the Nevada base, airmen saluted its last operational A-10 Warthog as it conducted its final flight Tuesday.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russian attack on Kyiv data centres affects number of internet providers.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russian attack on Kyiv data centres affects number of internet providers.
Domonet, Kievnet, and Faust reported infrastructure damage and internet outages in Kyiv following Russian strikes on local data centres on 24 September.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: Former commander-in-chief Zaluzhnyi: Russia continues to receive imported components, and could strike beyond Ukraine tomorrow.
Ukraine's Ambassador to UK Valerii Zaluzhnyi has warned that imported components for Russian weapons could enable strikes on other countries if not stopped.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Russian strike on a farm in Kharkiv Oblast: six killed, twelve injured – photos.
Russian forces struck a vegetable storage facility in Stara Hnylytsia, killing six farm workers and injuring 12, with four wounded hospitalised in a serious condition.
- The Moscow Times, 6 hours ago: Regions Calling: Russia’s Got a Bear Problem.
At least 19 people have been killed in brown bear attacks across the country since April. What is going on?
Southern Europe - bottom line: OpenAI’s agents went rogue — its human response caused the real damage.
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: OpenAI’s agents went rogue — its human response caused the real damage.
If you’ve been forwarded this newsletter, you can sign up free here. Confide in me: Send your tips to this generic inbox, canberraplaybook@poltico.com. - Balkan Insight, 9 hours ago: Kosovo Marks Banjska Attack Anniversary as Main Suspects Remain Free.
Politicians and relatives paid tribute to Kosovo police officer killed in September 2023 Banjska attack by an armed Serb gang, while the majority of the suspects remain at liberty, most likely in Serbia.
- Balkan Insight, 17 hours ago: Serbian Authorities Ridicule Spyware Attack Allegations Before Elections.
A month away from elections, Serbian authorities show no sign of investigating credible allegations that student protesters, politicians and activists have been targeted with spyware.
- Politico Europe, one hour ago: Europe grudgingly, gingerly moves toward Trump’s Board of Peace.
The European Commission is working with Trump’s body in Gaza for lack of better options. But the Board of Peace’s concrete results are slim.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Fighting intensifies in northern Ethiopia as Tigray rebels declare full-blown war.
- Africanews, 8 hours ago: Fighting intensifies in northern Ethiopia as Tigray rebels declare full-blown war.
Ethiopia’s army says its forces have killed 272 Tigrayan fighters and wounded 260 during a counter-offensive in Amhara. The press says the figures could not be independently verified.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 9 hours ago: Ethiopia: Ethiopia - Renewed Tigray Fighting Shows Need to Protect Civilians.
[HRW] Nairobi -- Fighting in Ethiopia's northern Tigray, Amhara, and Afar regions erupted on September 22, 2026, between the Ethiopian military and forces aligned with the Tigrayan People's Liberation Front, Tigray's main political party. This follows reported clashes and airstrikes in Tigray since August, including in Tigray's regional capital, Mekelle.
- Africanews, 13 hours ago: Tigray tensions rise as regional forces seize Mekelle airport.
The developments follow a series of reported drone strikes in Tigray. Regional authorities say at least 14 people were killed and 22 injured in a strike on the town of Alamata on Tuesday, with the mayor accusing federal forces of targeting schools.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 10 hours ago: Ethiopia: Attack By Rebel Group Raises Fear of Renewed War in Ethiopia.
[Premium Times] Months of rising tension in Ethiopia have now escalated into renewed armed clashes in the northern Tigray region, raising concerns that the country could slide back into a civil war.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Israel ready to resume strikes on Iran as regime aims to rebuild nuclear program - report.
- Jerusalem Post, 6 hours ago: Israel ready to resume strikes on Iran as regime aims to rebuild nuclear program - report.
"We will move to strike nuclear facilities and any site belonging to them again if Tehran crosses any of the red lines, whether with or without the participation of the US," an Israeli official said.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: Yemen's Houthis claim to have launched missiles, drones at Riyadh, Aramco facilities in Yanbu.
The statement came after Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis towards the southern province of Taif and Yanbu area on the Red Sea.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Ethiopian army says 272 Tigrayan fighters killed in Amhara.
Tigray People’s Liberation Front says in a 'situation of full-blown war' with Ethiopia's government.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: Twenty Gaza journalists removed from CPJ's war casualties list after combat roles uncovered.
CPJ maintains that affiliation with a militant organization is not sufficient for exclusion if a person was working as a civilian journalist and was not directly participating in hostilities.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 8 hours ago: Angola: Angolan Businessman Dinstinguished With Forbes Best of Africa Prize.
[ANGOP] New York -- Angolan businessman Edson dos Santos was distinguished on Tuesday (22), in New York (USA), with the Forbes Best of Africa Prize, at the Forbes Africa Day Award ceremony.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 12 hours ago: Namibia: Kahungu Cruises Towards Another Term.
[Namibian] Swapo Party Women's Council (SPWC) secretary Fransina Kahungu is set to return for another five-year term after being nominated unopposed to lead the women's wing at its upcoming ninth congress.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 12 hours ago: Malawi: World Bank Warns Malawi's Mining Potential Hinges On Solving Electricity Crisis.
[Nyasa Times] Malawi's drive to build a mining industry around critical minerals is being held back by a chronic electricity shortage, according to a new World Bank report that warns the country's mineral wealth could remain largely untapped without urgent power sector reform.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan conducted strikes at 10 locations in Afghanistan in response to recent drone attacks: info minister.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 13 hours ago: Pakistan conducted strikes at 10 locations in Afghanistan in response to recent drone attacks: info minister.
Pakistan has conducted precision aerial and drone strikes in 10 locations across Afghanistan in retaliation for drones launched from the neighbouring country a day earlier, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said in the early hours of Thursday. “In exercise of its sovereign right to self-defence, Pakistan conducted precision aerial and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan used for launching and storing these drones,” Tarar wrote in a post on social media platform X.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: Security forces kill several Afghan Taliban fighters in retaliatory action along Balochistan border: sources.
Pakistani troops responded to an act of aggression along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in Balochistan and killed several Afghan Taliban on Thursday, state media reported, citing sources. State-run APP reported, citing sources, that the Afghan Taliban attempted to enter the Pakistani territory in Balochistan’s Gulistan sector and carry out an act of aggression. The APP report said in retaliatory action, several Afghan Taliban fighters were killed. Intermittent exchange of fire between security forces and Afghan Taliban was ongoing after midnight, according the sources cited in the report.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: 8 terrorists killed in KP's North Waziristan: security sources.
Security forces killed eight terrorists in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan during an intelligence-based operation (IBO), security sources said on Thursday. The sources said the terrorists belonged to Fitna al Khawarij — a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). The hideouts used by the terrorists were also completely destroyed during the operation, according to security sources.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Pezeshkian says Islamabad MoU still 'fully acceptable' to Iran, ready to take it forward: PM Shehbaz.
WASHINGTON: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Thursday that Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian had told him the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was “fully acceptable” to Tehran even today and that they were “ready to take it forward”. The premier’s statement came after he held a “detailed” discussion with the Iranian president on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York.

- South China Morning Post - China, 13 hours ago: 8 killed in Russian strikes on Ukraine, maternity clinic damaged.
Russian drone and missile strikes on Ukraine’s capital Kyiv and its northeast killed eight people on Thursday in attacks that included a maternity hospital and a farm, officials said. Moscow has stepped up its air ‌war in recent months, deploying more of its faster and harder-to-stop drones while Ukraine is short of interceptors to down ballistic missiles. Two people died in the latest assault on Kyiv, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky, who was in New York for the UN General...

China and the United States must prevent their AI competition from escalating into a cold war, a top Chinese policy adviser has warned, while asserting that a complete decoupling would be difficult. The remarks from Zheng Yongnian, a leading political scientist and dean of the school of public policy at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, come ahead of the Xi-Trump summit in Washington, where artificial intelligence (AI) is expected to be among the top items on the agenda. Chinese...

A man armed with a knife killed a priest and injured four other people during an attack on clergy and worshippers at a Benedictine abbey in southern Poland on Thursday, authorities ‌said. The man used a knife he took from a kitchen there to attack one woman and four men, including one priest who was in a confessional, a prosecutor said. The attack took place at a Benedictine Sisters monastery on the grounds of the abbey in Jaroslaw, local media reported. A 31-year-old Ukrainian man was arrested,...
- South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: Netanyahu, at UN, calls accusations of genocide in Gaza ‘the biggest lie of the century’.
Allegations of Israeli genocide in Gaza are not only false but “the biggest lie of the century”, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told world leaders on Thursday in a defiant speech that asserted his nation’s right to wage war against Iran – a speech that was not heard by scores of delegates who trooped out before he started speaking. - Times of India - Top Stories, 9 hours ago: Did AI-‘kill chain’ lead to deadly Iran school strike? What report claims.
A devastating missile strike by the US on a school in Minab, Iran, has led to the tragic loss of over 150 lives, including 123 innocent children. - NK News, 14 hours ago: North Korea slams ‘unrealistic’ calls for denuclearization by US, ROK, Japan.
North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui on Thursday rejected a joint call by the United States, South Korea and Japan for Pyongyang to denuclearize and return to dialogue, saying the country remains “unchanged in its will to keep nuclear weapons forever.” In a statement released through the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), Choe […]

After lobbying for years for a permanent war memorial, residents of Coral Bay have been told to make do with a transportable one by a government department.

Speaking to scores of empty chairs after a mass walkout, Benjamin Netanyahu uses his UN speech to lavish praise on Donald Trump, savage Zohran Mamdani and predict Iran's population will topple its ruling regime.
